explanation: The I50V mutation in the flap region reduces a critical hydrophobic contact with lopinavir through loss of ~27 Ų of van der Waals surface area, weakening the enthalpic contribution of the inhibitor-binding pocket interaction despite the short 2.2 Å contact distance. The smaller valine side chain creates a hydrophobic cavity that cannot be optimally filled by lopinavir's corresponding binding surface, diminishing favorable dispersion interactions that normally stabilize the protease-inhibitor complex. This localized loss of van der Waals complementarity at the flap-ligand interface, though modest in energetic terms (~0.1 kcal/mol), represents a direct reduction in binding affinity that favors viral escape.
